topIssues.title: Path C: SFDG → SZKDG
topIssues.author: ashitakah
topIssues.body:
## Goal

Multiple chains share a single DGF, ASR, and ETHLockbox post-interop.
`OPCMv2.upgrade()` was designed for one chain at a time.

## Options (pending resolution during Tech Design)

1. **Idempotent reinitialization**: ASR reinitializer safe to apply twice,
   second call is no-op for shared contracts. Requires careful design around
   OZ `reinitializer(uint8)` guards.
2. **Multi-chain bulk function**: takes multiple `SystemConfig`s, upgrades
   shared infrastructure once, handles per-chain state in a loop.

## Blocking
Design approach must be resolved during Tech Design.

## Definition of Done
- Approach chosen and implemented
- Tests passing including in-flight withdrawal backward compatibility

## Weekly Updates

**[YYYY-MM-DD]** <latest update>

topPRs.title: docs: add cross-repo link policy page and CI link-policy linter
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#962 · Plan: [option-b-truth-from-source.md, slice B2](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/blob/main/projects/docs-improver/plans/option-b-truth-from-source.md) · Program docs: [projects/docs-improver/README.md](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/tree/main/projects/docs-improver)

## What / why

The docs↔specs↔source link graph rots silently: retired spec paths keep "working" only through a hand-maintained redirect table in the specs repo's `book.toml`, UTM decoration pasted after an anchor breaks the fragment without breaking the page, and commit-pinned contract links never 404 while teaching a two-generations-old architecture. This PR ships the policy that names the canonical form for every cross-repo link, and the deterministic CI linter that enforces it.

### Before

* No written link policy; link form re-litigated (or unnoticed) per PR.
* On `develop` today the linter finds **368 violations**: 291 unbadged sha-/tag-pinned source links (47 pages), 51 retired `/experimental/`-era spec paths, 12 GitHub-blob links into specs sources, 7 query-after-fragment anchors, 3 dead internal links, 2 malformed link targets, 2 unresolved spec anchors.
* No CI gate: any docs PR can add more of each class.

### After

* **Policy page** `op-stack/contribute/link-policy.mdx` (`/op-stack/contribute/link-policy`): rendered specs.optimism.io on current paths; UTM before the `#fragment`; GitHub-blob spec links banned where a rendered page exists; sha-/tag-pins only with an ``as of `` `` badge; deep spec anchors must resolve; root-relative internal links. Written as an annex of the content guide (optimism#21841).
* **Linter** `docs/public-docs/scripts/lint-link-policy.mjs`: dependency-free Node script; vendors the specs `book.toml` redirect table for retired-path detection; resolves spec paths and anchors against a checkout of `ethereum-optimism/specs` using mdBook slug rules; detects dead internal links honoring `docs.json` redirects.
* **Baseline** `scripts/lint-link-policy.baseline.json`: all current findings recorded so **CI blocks only NEW violations** and is green at introduction. The baseline is the burn-down worklist for the follow-up remediation sweep.
* **Fixtures** `docs/lint-link-policy-fixtures/`: one failing fixture per violation class + passing fixtures + a hermetic specs stand-in, run via `--self-test` in CI. Kept outside the Mintlify content root so the deliberate violations never appear in `mint broken-links` output.
* **CI** `.github/workflows/docs-link-policy.yml` (new file, path-filtered to the docs tree): self-test → specs clone → baselined lint; plus `mint broken-links` as an **advisory** job (`continue-on-error`) until the sweep clears the 5 pre-existing broken links recorded on ethereum-optimism/solutions#954 — flip it to blocking then.
* One-line fix: `node-operators/guides/configuration/consensus-clients.mdx` now points at the in-site kona book (`/rust/kona/intro/overview`) instead of the retired external kona book site.

## Verification

* `node scripts/lint-link-policy.mjs --self-test`: all 8 violation classes fire on their failing fixture; passing fixtures are clean.
* Full-tree run against `develop` with specs resolution: 368 findings, all baselined; run exits 0. A canary file with a retired spec path + dead internal link makes the baselined run exit 1 (verified, then removed).
* All 5 pre-existing `mint broken-links` findings from ethereum-optimism/solutions#954 are accounted for: 3 caught as `dead-internal-link`, 1 as `malformed-link`; the 5th (`/operators/chain-operators`) resolves via an explicit `docs.json` redirect, so the linter treats it as alive by design (the sweep should still re-point it).
* `mint broken-links` run locally after moving the fixtures out of the content root: reports only the 5 pre-existing links plus this page's forward-link to the content guide.
* **Specs anchor resolution note:** outbound access to specs.optimism.io is blocked from this session, so spec paths/anchors were resolved against the `ethereum-optimism/specs` repo source (mirrored via raw.githubusercontent.com) — the same thing the CI job does with a real `git clone`. The vendored retired-path table matches the current `book.toml` redirect table.

## docs.json lane

This PR adds a `Contribute` group at the end of the OP Stack tab containing only the policy page. **Synced with develop after #21841 merged; the policy page now sits in the merged Contribute group** (after `content-guide`). The baseline entry that covered this page's forward-link to `/op-stack/contribute/content-guide` was pruned in the sync — the target now exists in-tree — and the self-test + baselined run were re-verified green.

## Out of scope (held, per plan sequencing)

* The **~90-page mechanical remediation sweep** (retired-path rewrites, anchor+UTM fixes, blob→rendered canonicalization, pin badging) — gated on this linter merging so the sweep runs against a merged, trusted check; the committed baseline is its worklist, to be burned down in serialized batches.
* The **bridging-explainer re-point** (`op-stack/bridging/deposit-flow.mdx`, `withdrawal-flow.mdx` off 2023 v1.1.4 links) — optimism#21593 (deposit-flow split) is still in review and touches the same files; runs after it resolves, with an accuracy pass against current `OptimismPortal2`-era contracts.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Policy rules match how we actually want links written (especially the ``as of `` `` badge convention for deliberate pins)
- [ ] `docs.json` hunk is the agreed Contribute-group position (now merged into #21841's group)
- [ ] Baseline-gating is acceptable: pre-existing violations pass, new ones block
- [ ] Advisory (non-blocking) status for `mint broken-links` is acceptable until the sweep lands
- [ ] Workflow file: path filters, pinned actions, permissions

topPRs.title: docs: add hardfork registry and regroup notices into release-train framing
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#970

## What

One permanent registry page per OP Stack hardfork (Regolith → Lagoon) with structured frontmatter — lifecycle, superchain-default activation timestamps, governing spec link, governance approval, minimum component versions — plus `scripts/generate-hardforks.ts`, which validates the schema, cross-checks every activation against the superchain-registry configs, and renders the generated activation tables under `snippets/generated/hardforks/` (`pnpm gen:hardforks` / `gen:hardforks:check`). A frontmatter edit is the only way to change an activation row.

`op-stack/protocol/network-upgrades.mdx` becomes the registry index: its hand-maintained table (already stale — the Karst row still said "pending / TBD" after the 2026-07-08 mainnet activation) is replaced by the generated summary. The Notices tab is regrouped into Network Upgrades / Deprecations / Operations with **no URL moves and no new redirects**; the notices overview now frames notices as transient action items and the registry as the permanent record.

Shared artifact: this is the single hardfork-registry implementation shared by the Option B (slice B4) and Option A (slice 6) docs programs — A6 consumes these pages, the schema check, and the generated tables.

## Why

Upgrade facts were scattered across Notices, per-page banners, and a hand-edited table that had already drifted. Facts that change often now live in structured data validated against source (superchain-registry); prose lives in pages.

## Source citations

*   Activation timestamps: `superchain-registry` `superchain/configs/{mainnet,sepolia}/superchain.toml`; Regolith's genesis activation: `rust/alloy-op-hardforks/src/optimism/{mainnet,sepolia}.rs`; Bedrock anchor: registry `mainnet/op.toml [genesis]` (block `105235063`, timestamp `1686068903` — corrects the old page's `1686079703`, which contradicted its own block arithmetic).
*   Spec links: `ethereum-optimism/specs` `specs/protocol/<fork>/overview.md` (all 11 verified; deep anchors resolved against spec headings); rendered-site links per the cross-repo link policy.
*   Minimum versions: the Upgrade 19 / 17 / 15 and Holocene notices in this repo, cited on each page.

## Verification

An independent adversarial accuracy pass re-derived every claim before this PR opened: all 18 activation rows re-checked against a fresh read of superchain-registry `main` @ `738212ef2932d26f9274e3317699471534d2b3ac` (the same commit the monorepo submodule pins); block estimates recomputed from the genesis anchors; spec overviews and deep anchors re-fetched from `ethereum-optimism/specs@main`; min-version tables re-checked against the in-repo notices; `gen:hardforks:check` confirmed to fail on a deliberately corrupted timestamp and on a registry fork with no page, and the committed snippets confirmed byte-identical to a fresh regeneration.

## Nav / serialization note

This PR touches `docs.json` (Protocol Information group + Notices regroup). Per the docs.json serialized lane it rebases on demand as other nav PRs merge; its two hunks do not overlap the docs.json regions touched by the currently open docs-improver nav PRs. Nav validator, redirect lint, and link-policy linter are green with zero baseline/allowlist growth; `mint broken-links` reports only the 5 findings already present on `develop`.

## Reviewer checklist

*   [ ] Spot-check two activation rows against the superchain-registry
*   [ ] `pnpm gen:hardforks:check` passes (requires the superchain-registry submodule or `--registry`)
*   [ ] Notices regroup reads correctly (no URL moves intended)
*   [ ] Follow-up (not this PR): the Upgrade 19 notice still describes Karst as "proposed / pending governance approval" post-activation — it should be refreshed/archived

See `projects/docs-improver/README.md` for program context.

topPRs.title: feat: migration path C zkdg
topPRs.author: ashitakah
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds the interop migration path (Path C): `OPContractsManagerV2.setInteropDisputeGames(...)`, which re-points the shared dispute games of an already-interop set to a new respected super game in a single transaction covering all chains. Current use case is the post-migration transition from shared fault proofs to a shared super `ZKDisputeGame`. Reuses the migrator machinery; the standard `upgrade()` path can't be used since it re-inits per chain and would clobber the shared `AnchorStateRegistry` / `ETHLockbox`. Paths A and B (isolated chains) need no contract changes and go through `upgrade()`, since ZK is already in `isSuperGame`.

## Changes

### Contracts — `src/L1/opcm/OPContractsManagerMigrator.sol`

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `setInteropDisputeGames` | New function. Validates the chain set, re-initializes the shared `AnchorStateRegistry` with the new respected game type + anchor root, then sets the dispute game impls on the shared `DisputeGameFactory` via the existing `_getGameImpl` / `_makeGameArgs`. Enabled configs register, disabled configs clear. No new infra deployed, per-chain portals untouched. |
| Guards | Gates on `OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP` + `ZK_DISPUTE_GAME` dev features (TODO to drop the ZK gate once finalized; the function is generic across super games). Requires `startingRespectedGameType ∈ isSuperGame`. Runtime check that all portals resolve to the same shared ASR. |
| Errors | `OPContractsManagerMigrator_ZKDisputeGameNotEnabled`, `OPContractsManagerMigrator_NotSharedInteropSet`. |

### Contracts — `src/L1/opcm/OPContractsManagerV2.sol`

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `setInteropDisputeGames` | Thin entry point, `_onlyDelegateCall` + delegatecall to the migrator (mirrors `migrate()`). Transitional, removed once interop is native in OPCM. |
| Version | `7.1.22` → `7.1.23`. |

### Interfaces

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `interfaces/L1/opcm/IOPContractsManagerMigrator.sol` | Added `setInteropDisputeGames` + the two errors. |
| `interfaces/L1/opcm/IOPContractsManagerV2.sol` | Added `setInteropDisputeGames`. |

### Forge script — `scripts/deploy/SetInteropDisputeGames.s.sol`

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Script | New `Input` / `Output` / `run` mirroring `InteropMigration.s.sol`. Etches `DummyCaller` to simulate the governance delegatecall. `checkOutput` asserts on chain: all portals share the DGF, respected game type updated, and each input config applied (enabled registered, disabled cleared). |

### Op-deployer (Go)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage/set_interop_dispute_games.go` | `SetInteropDisputeGames` runner, `encodeZKGameArgs` (5-field ZK config), `SetInteropDisputeGamesCLI`. Validates all address flags with `IsHexAddress`. Default clears only `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` (9, the permissionless slot ZK replaces) and keeps `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` (5) as the permissioned liveness backup. |
| `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage/flags.go` | New flags (`--system-config-proxy-addresses`, `--source-game-types`, `--zk-verifier-address`, `--zk-max-challenge-duration`, `--zk-max-prove-duration`) + `set-interop-dispute-games` command. |

### Tests

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `test/L1/opcm/OPContractsManagerV2.t.sol` | `test_setInteropDisputeGames_succeeds` (migrate to interop with SPDG + kona, swap to ZK, asserts SPDG kept, ZK registered + respected, kona cleared), `_notDelegateCalled_reverts`, `_notSharedInteropSet_reverts`. |
| `op-deployer/pkg/deployer/manage/set_interop_dispute_games_test.go` | `TestEncodeZKGameArgs` (encoder round-trip + validation), `TestSetInteropDisputeGames` (forked-Sepolia e2e: deploy with ZK impl, migrate to interop, swap, asserts the end shape on chain). |

### Snapshots

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `snapshots/semver-lock.json`, `snapshots/abi/*` | Regenerated for the OPCMv2 version bump and the new `setInteropDisputeGames` ABI. |

### Notes

- Target post-swap shape is `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` (permissioned backup) + `ZK_DISPUTE_GAME` (permissionless, respected), mirroring today's permissioned + permissionless super shape.
- Paths A and B (single-chain `SPDG`/`SFDG` → ZK) and full game-lifecycle / finalization tests are handled in the integration tests PR.
- No on-chain validator covers the post-swap state yet (StandardValidator super-mode is gated on `SUPER_ROOT_GAMES_MIGRATION`; MigrationValidator requires the cannon super types). Tracked with the `ZKDG-NOSHAPE` TODO.
- op-challenger ZK actor needs interop super-root handling + the invalid-parent challenge fix (#21445) before the games can be defended in production.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20759

topPRs.title: docs: generate deploy-config schema reference from source, keyed to finalized op-deployer releases
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#972

## What

Replaces the hand-transcribed `DeployConfig` catalog on
`chain-operators/reference/rollup-deployment-configuration.mdx` with a schema
generated from the `DeployConfig` struct tree in `op-chain-ops/genesis` at the
newest finalized op-deployer release (`op-deployer/v0.7.1`), imported as a
snippet. Hand-maintained guidance (Standard Rollup Charter requirements,
recommended values) stays on the page around the generated tables.

New generator: `docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-deploy-config/` — an AST-based
sibling of `scripts/gen-flags/` reusing its conventions (do-not-edit header,
provenance line, `manifest.json` with `{tag, sha256}`, `-check` mode). It
parses source rather than building it, so it generates at a release tag
directly; it fails loudly on any struct/type/tag it cannot map, so upstream
schema changes force a conscious docs decision instead of silent drift.

## Why

This page hand-transcribed Go structs and drifted the way every hand catalog
does (slice B5 of the Truth-from-Source plan, `projects/docs-improver/plans/
option-b-truth-from-source.md` in ethereum-optimism/solutions):

- 3 documented fields no longer exist in the struct (`useInterop`,
  `l2GenesisBlockExtraData`, `numDeployConfirmations`)
- ~50 real fields were missing (Granite→Karst activation offsets, custom gas
  token, operator fee, L1 BPO offsets, dev L1 genesis)
- wrong types: fee-vault withdrawal networks are `"remote"`/`"local"` strings
  (legacy 0/1 accepted on input; re-emitted as 0/1), documented as plain
  `0`/`1` numbers; `l1StartingBlockTag` is a number/tag/hash, documented as
  "Block hash"

The generated schema is 122 values in 20 groups, each traceable to a struct
field at the tag. The schema documents the release, not `develop` — the tag's
`l2GenesisInteropTimeOffset` appears (renamed to Lagoon on `develop` after the
release), and develop-only `keepKarstUpgradeGas` does not, by design.

## Verification (independent adversarial pass)

An adversarial verifier re-derived the schema with its own extraction method
(independent of the generator's go/ast walk) and exercised the tooling:

- `op-deployer/v0.7.1` confirmed as the newest finalized non-rc/non-alpha
  op-deployer tag via `git ls-remote --tags origin 'op-deployer/*'`
- 122/122 JSON keys, row order (encoding/json flattening order), group↔struct
  boundaries, and all 15 Go-type→label mappings match the independent
  extraction from `config.go` at the tag; the 3 removed fields do not exist at
  the tag
- `WithdrawalNetwork` semantics verified against `Valid()`/`ToUint8()`/
  `MarshalJSON` in `withdrawal_network.go`
- Regeneration from the tag source is byte-identical to the committed snippet;
  `-check` against develop's moved-on tree reports the divergence
  informationally; a corrupted snippet byte fails `-check` on sha256; an
  unmapped field type fails generation loudly without writing
- `go vet` + `gofmt` clean; nav validator, redirect lint, and link-policy
  linter (with baseline + specs mirror) all pass with zero new findings;
  `docs.json` untouched; zero file overlap with #21873
- Verifier follow-up commit (620949d6c): restored three curated `address(0)`
  constraints the rework had dropped (each mirrors a `Check()` error in the
  source), fixed two dead `network-upgrades#fjord`/`#granite` anchors carried
  from the old page, updated the guardian guidance from the removed Deputy
  Guardian Module spec section to the current Deputy Pause Module (clearing
  the one baselined spec-anchor finding this page carried), and noted the
  legacy numeric re-marshal form of the withdrawal-network values

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Spot-check a few generated rows against `op-chain-ops/genesis/config.go`
      at `op-deployer/v0.7.1`
- [ ] Confirm the hand guidance section preserved the standard-configuration
      requirements you care about (one stale item was intentionally dropped:
      the old `l1CancunTimeOffset` "recommended 0x0" guidance)
